title: Trust, acceptance and use of AI functions in practice management software systems – opportunities for research and development
summary:
Digital practice management systems form the technological backbone of outpatient medical care in Germany. With the advent of digitally supported administrative and medical processes, including AI-powered functions such as automated documentation, decision support, and organizational assistance, there is potential to make care processes more efficient and reduce workloads.

Despite these technological developments, practice shows that many of these functions are currently only used to a limited extent. Reasons for this may include uncertainties in using the technology, a lack of trust, and varying levels of user acceptance.

The study "Trust, Acceptance, and Use of AI-Supported Functions in Outpatient Practice Management Systems" (VANKIP) therefore investigates how physicians and medical assistants perceive, evaluate, and use such digitally supported processes and which factors influence trust, acceptance, and actual use. The aim is to develop practical recommendations for a user-centered and trust-building design and implementation of such processes.
